about: Sweating Bullets is a close-up of Jordan Peele with his face completely drenched: streams of sweat run down his forehead, nose and cheeks while he stares off to the side with a tense, frozen expression. The absurd amount of sweat is the whole point. It is the face of someone who is about to be found out, is watching a plan fall apart in real time, or is holding a secret under pressure. People use it for any moment of extreme nervousness, especially when the stakes are small but feel enormous.
origin: The frame comes from a sketch on Key & Peele, the Comedy Central sketch show starring Keegan-Michael Key and Jordan Peele.
usage:
Use the top box for the setup and the bottom box for the nerve-wracking detail, or split one "when..." sentence across both: "when the demo" / "is on prod". The face is the punchline, so the text should describe the moment just before disaster.

Classic setups: a teacher asks for homework you didn't do, a manager says "quick chat?", someone opens your search history, the cashier reruns your card. Exaggerated panic over everyday stakes fits the over-the-top sweat best.
